text:
Southern maize leaf blight (Bipolaris maydis, also known as Helminthosporium maydis).

Symptoms: tan to brown, elongated, spindle- or eye-shaped leaf lesions, typically 2-3 cm long, running parallel to the leaf veins. In severe infections, lesions merge and blight large areas of the leaf, reducing photosynthesis; the disease can also affect the ear and husk under heavy pressure.

Management: resistant varieties are the primary control measure; fungicide can be considered where infection is severe. Crop rotation and residue management help reduce the amount of disease inoculum carried over between seasons, and avoiding overly dense planting (which reduces airflow and raises humidity in the canopy) also helps limit disease development.
